paras: The threatened lynching of George Ostrander occurred at Nebraska City, Nebraska, on the night of August 3, 1888, when a mob called for a rope as officers arrested Ostrander, a painter accused of beating his teenage daughter. Officers hurried him to jail and he was not harmed.

Ostrander was accused of beating his sixteen-year-old daughter into unconsciousness and leaving her head and body covered in bruises. According to the Nebraska City telegram to the Omaha Daily Bee, neighbors interfered and cared for the girl, and the correspondent wrote that he would otherwise have killed her. A later state-news brief said her life was in danger. Ostrander, as the Bee reported his account, said the cause was that the daughter and her mother were "too conspicuous upon the streets after night."

When Ostrander was arrested, a mob that had assembled raised cries for "a rope." The Bee's correspondent wrote that had the officers not hustled him off he would have been "roughly handled," while the Red Cloud Chief said he was followed to jail by a mob "yelling for a rope" and would have "fared badly" without the officers' care. Neither report gives the size of the crowd, names any of its members, or states Ostrander's race.
Ostrander was lodged in jail, and no arrests of mob members were reported. No report of a hearing, trial, or the daughter's recovery appears in the coverage.

The Omaha Daily Bee carried the first report on August 4 as a special telegram from Nebraska City under the headline "Beat His Daughter Brutally," placed among other Nebraska dispatches. Its account dwelt on the girl's injuries, gave the mob a single sentence, and closed with Ostrander's own explanation. On August 10 the Red Cloud Chief ran a one-paragraph version in its column of state news, dating the arrest only to "the other night" and crediting the officers with saving him. Neither paper commented on the mob or on the case in an editorial.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of George Ostrander
bases: A mob called for a rope against a man under arrest, a threatened lynching that officers prevented by hurrying him away (A1, A2).
Ostrander was not harmed; a mob of unstated size called for a rope over his alleged beating of his daughter, but officers got him to jail (A1, A2).

Two Nebraska papers in differently worded items agree on the arrest, the accusation, the mob's cries for a rope and the officers' protection (A1, A2); the later brief may be condensed from earlier reports rather than independently gathered.
